title: Ulyana and the Wolf
premise: Paloma Okonkwo, a mercenary whose god of contracts has gone silent for a decade, survives by knowing every smuggler's road through the Thornfell mountains and trusting no one. When a dying courier presses a map into her hands, she learns the map leads to the court beneath the mountain, where a stolen soul—Ulyana's—is held as collateral for an ancient debt owed by Paloma's own dead mentor. Hunted by the mountain's tithe-collectors and shadowed by Ulyana, a wolf-shifter who remembers nothing of what she sold, Paloma must decide whether justice outside the law is worth breaking her last vow. In the end she trades her own silence-god contract to buy Ulyana's soul back, extinguishing the last dragon-fire that keeps the under-court alive—and walks out of Thornfell with a found family instead of a god.
about_author: Vesper Okafor is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons mapping passes in the Carpathians before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about debts, borders, and the people who slip between them.

chapters.title: The God Who Stopped Answering
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. On a rain-slicked smuggler's road, Paloma completes a routine escort job and performs her nightly prayer to a god who hasn't spoken in ten years. The beat establishes her isolation, competence, and quiet grief over the broken contract that defines her.

chapters.title: Blood on the Switchback
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A dying courier collapses at her campfire, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and whispering 'the tithe comes due' before expiring. Tithe-collectors arrive minutes later; Paloma kills two and flees. Beat: terror—the invisible life is over.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Hiding in a burned-out shrine, Paloma deciphers the map: routes into the court beneath the mountain, annotated in her dead mentor Ilya's handwriting. She realizes he sold something there. Beat: betrayal from beyond the grave.

chapters.title: The Wolf at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. At a river crossing she's ambushed by a huge grey wolf that shifts mid-leap into a naked, terrified young woman—Ulyana—who recognizes the map and begs for it back. Beat: reluctant alliance; Paloma can't bring herself to abandon her.

chapters.title: Ulyana
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. We learn Ulyana sold her soul-memories to the under-court to save her pack, and remembers only fragments—a sister's laugh, a burning den. She needs the map to find what she lost. Beat: vulnerability meeting Paloma's armor.

chapters.title: Tithe-Collectors
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The collectors corner them in a market town; a bargain broker named Sef offers Paloma amnesty if she surrenders the map and the girl. Paloma refuses, burning a bridge she can't rebuild. Beat: first open choice of loyalty.

chapters.title: Roads Only Smugglers Know
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A travel chapter through hidden passes, salt caves, and a hermit's bridge. Paloma teaches Ulyana survival; Ulyana's warmth begins cracking Paloma's solitude. Beat: found family taking root in small gestures.

chapters.title: The Heretic's Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Sheltering in a chapel to Paloma's silent god, Ulyana finds records of other souls sold below—including children. Paloma admits Ilya brokered such deals. Beat: shared outrage hardens into purpose; this becomes about justice, not escape.

chapters.title: Sef's Price
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Sef captures them, revealing the under-court pays in years of life, and offers Ulyana's freedom if Paloma delivers the map alone. Paloma pretends to accept. Beat: moral compromise; the reader fears she might mean it.

chapters.title: Fire in the High Pass
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Sef betrays them anyway; a dragon-fire beacon lit on the pass signals the under-court. Ulyana shifts fully to save Paloma, losing more memories in the process—she forgets Paloma's name. Beat: sacrifice and heartbreak.

chapters.title: Ilya's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. In Ilya's hidden cache, Paloma finds his ledger: he sold his own soul to guarantee hers would never be taken, and the debt transfers to her on his death. Beat: devastating revelation—she was always the collateral.

chapters.title: The Gate Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. They reach the mountain gate, guarded by a door that asks each entrant their truest want. Ulyana answers 'my sister'; Paloma cannot answer and bleeds for entry instead. Beat: dread and intimacy at the threshold.

chapters.title: Court of Quiet Bells
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Inside, the under-court is beautiful and wrong: a frozen feast, nobles wearing borrowed faces, dragon-fire guttering in a central brazier. Ulyana glimpses her own soul in a glass reliquary. Beat: wonder curdling to horror.

chapters.title: The Bargain Broker's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Sef arrives to collect, revealing the court's law: one soul may be redeemed only by an equal pledge. Paloma offers Ilya's ledger-debt—herself—in exchange. Beat: the vow breaks; she chooses Ulyana over self-preservation.

chapters.title: A Sister in Glass
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Searching the reliquary vaults, Ulyana finds not only her soul but her living sister, kept as the court's cupbearer, memory-wiped like the rest. Beat: hope and rage; the stakes widen beyond one soul.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. An ancient chained dragon reveals the truth: the court runs on its dying fire, and every soul sold feeds it. When the fire gutters out, all stolen souls go free—but the mountain falls. Beat: impossible arithmetic of justice.

chapters.title: What Silence Costs
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma attempts to void her god-contract to free herself for the trade, and the silent god finally answers—not with words but with acceptance, releasing her. Beat: grief transmuted; she loses the last thing tying her to her old life.

chapters.title: The Feast Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. During the court's centennial tithe-feast, Ulyana and freed captives sabotage the reliquaries while Paloma confronts the Lord Beneath. Beat: rising chaos, plan fraying, courage anyway.

chapters.title: Climax: The Pledge
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Paloma seals the trade—her pledged soul for Ulyana's—as the dragon-fire dies. The court begins collapsing; the Lord Beneath tries to renege, and the released souls themselves drag him down. Beat: climax—sacrifice answered by collective justice.

chapters.title: When the Mountain Falls
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Escape through disintegrating tunnels, the freed dragon carrying stragglers out. Ulyana refuses to leave without Paloma, who is fading as her pledge takes hold. Beat: desperation, loyalty tested against death.

chapters.title: The Wolf's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Outside, Ulyana splits her restored soul—giving half willingly to Paloma—because a soul freely given cancels a soul forcibly pledged. The old law has no answer for a gift. Beat: love as the loophole; Paloma wakes.

chapters.title: Roads Forward
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Spring in the foothills: Ulyana reunited with her sister, refugees resettling, the dragon ranging free. Paloma prays once more—to no one, or to everyone—and gets up off her knees smiling. Beat: resolution; family chosen, justice carried, roads open.
